scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Velocity-Field Detection of Computation in Forced Navier–Stokes Flows” (preprints/Velocity-Field-Detection-of-Computation-in-Forced-Navier-Stokes-Flows-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a69fca6b458f542a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each positive computable ν, a machine and a finite input effectively determine each of the following two forces. 1. On T3, a smooth force has a unique global smooth solution in the torus class above, with pressure zero, for which (2) holds exactly when the machine halts. The force is supported in K × T for a compact K ⊂ (0, 1)2 independent of time. Its derivatives are bounded on every finite time interval; their bounds may grow with that interval. 2. On R2 × T, a smooth force and all its mixed derivatives are globally bounded. On each finite time interval its horizontal support is compact. It has a unique global smooth solution in (4), with pressure zero and integrable nonnegative third component. Event (3) holds exactly when the machine halts. The sets and thresholds in both observations are independent of the machine and input. The compact set K in the first construction may depend on that instance, but is independent of time. Both force prescriptions install all the required local instructions, without executing the selected computation.
